properties.name: Cosmopolis
properties.legend_label: Closed, closure year verified

properties.name: Hutchinson
properties.legend_label: Closed, closure year verified
properties.note: Paperboard mill opened 1909; Sonoco (owner since 2001, via acquisition from Republic Group) abruptly closed the 90,000-ton/yr mill in March 2023, laying off 116 workers.

properties.name: Old Town
properties.legend_label: Idled or largely shut
properties.note: Historic Penobscot River pulp mill (papermaking here dates to 1882) was shuttered by prior owner Expera in 2015; ND Paper/Nine Dragons bought the site in 2018 and restarted it as a recycled bleached-kraft pulp mill in 2019; idled indefinitely in April 2023 citing high fiber and energy costs and has not restarted since.

properties.name: Putney
properties.company: Marcal Paper Mills, Inc. (previously Soundview Paper Company)
properties.legend_label: Closed, closure year verified
properties.note: Tissue-making at this Sacketts Brook site dates to 1869 (Eagle Paper Mill), on a mill site used for papermaking since the early 1800s; operated most recently as Soundview/Putney Paper (Marcal brand), producing recycled tissue parent rolls; papermaking stopped Jan. 16, 2024 (the separate converting operation ran a few more weeks) after energy costs became unsustainable.

properties.name: Saint Helens
properties.legend_label: Closed, closure year verified
properties.note: St. Helens Pulp and Paper Mill was built by Crown Zellerbach (its 50th anniversary was marked in 1977); Cascades began recycled-tissue production at the site in 2002; Cascades shut its remaining paper machine and fully closed the plant in Oct. 2023 amid weak West Coast demand for brown recycled tissue.

properties.name: South Glens Falls
properties.legend_label: Closed, closure year verified
properties.note: Tissue mill on the Hudson River built 1883-84; Essity abruptly closed it in July 2023, consolidating US tissue production at other sites and affecting roughly 300 area jobs.

properties.name: Sumner
properties.legend_label: Closed, closure year verified
properties.note: Uncoated recycled paperboard (URB) mill running since 1915 (Sonoco-owned since 1980); Sonoco permanently closed the 40,000-ton/yr mill effective Feb. 5, 2024, citing network optimization.

properties.name: Tacoma
properties.legend_label: Closed, closure year verified
properties.note: Kraft pulp and paper mill (linerboard, kraft bag paper) built 1929 by St. Regis Paper Co.; passed through Champion, Simpson Paper and RockTenn to WestRock; WestRock permanently closed the 510,000-ton/yr mill in Sept. 2023 after 94 years, citing high operating costs.

properties.name: Tama
properties.legend_label: Closed, closure year verified
properties.note: Paperboard mill opened 1878 (originally straw-based, later 100% recycled box board); Graphic Packaging closed the small, high-cost-per-ton mill on June 2, 2023, after 144+ years, as part of a network simplification.

properties.name: Port Angeles (Nippon Paper)
properties.company: Grupo Bio PAPPEL, S.A.B. de C.V. (McKinley Paper Co.)
properties.legend_label: Closed, closure year verified
properties.note: A genuinely distinct facility from the Rayonier pulp mill (1930-1997) elsewhere in Port Angeles: this integrated pulp/paper mill at Ediz Hook was built in 1920 by Crown Zellerbach, passed to Daishowa America (1988) and then Nippon Paper Industries; Nippon sold it to McKinley Paper Co. (a Grupo Bio Pappel subsidiary) in 2017, and McKinley permanently closed the mill in mid-2024 (60-day WARN notice issued late June 2024) citing recovered-paper costs and weak demand.

properties.name: Westervelt (Gulf States Paper)
properties.company: Westervelt Co. (formerly Gulf States Paper Corp.)
properties.legend_label: Closed, closure year approximate
properties.review_reasons: open year uncertain; close year estimated
properties.note: Built by Gulf States Paper Corp. as Alabama's first paper mill; made bleached kraft pulp and paper; in operation about 50 years before closing in the mid-1970s (exact year not confirmed, hence 1975 estimate). Parent company continued as Westervelt Co. in forest products/real estate after the mill closed.

properties.name: Crossett
properties.legend_label: No closure recorded (operating status not confirmed)
properties.note: Kraft pulp/paper mill built 1937 by Crossett Lumber Co.; Georgia-Pacific bought the site in 1962. Bleached board production ended in 2019 with a shift toward tissue/towel, but the pulp mill and chemical plant continue operating.

properties.name: Los Angeles Paper Box & Board Mill
properties.company: Los Angeles Paper Box & Board Mills Inc.
properties.legend_label: No closure recorded (operating status not confirmed)
properties.note: Family-owned recycled paperboard mill and folding-carton/box plant; still operating in Commerce, CA (LA metro area).

properties.name: Simkins Industries (New Haven Pulp & Paper)
properties.legend_label: Closed, closure year verified
properties.note: Originally New Haven Pulp & Paper Co.; recycled old newspapers into paperboard and specialty papers (Deerfield Specialty Papers & Glassine Canada brand). Permanently closed on or about Aug. 25, 2006 after years of losses and a failed contract-concession vote.

properties.name: Atlas Paper Mills
properties.company: Atlas Paper Mills Ltd. (Atlas Paper Mills LLC)
properties.legend_label: No closure recorded (operating status not confirmed)
properties.note: Founded by Remberto Bastanzuri, a Cuban paper-industry veteran who arrived in Miami in 1979; sources differ on the exact founding year (1979-1982). Recycled-fiber tissue mill actually located in Hialeah (Miami-Dade County), not a specific city named in the old directory; still operating.

properties.name: Roses SouthEast Papers
properties.legend_label: No closure recorded (operating status not confirmed)
properties.note: Recycled/virgin tissue mill (bath tissue, towels, napkins); acquired by a Peak Rock Capital affiliate in 2014 and rebranded Atlas Southeast Papers; still operating.

properties.name: Caraustar Austell
properties.legend_label: No closure recorded (operating status not confirmed)
properties.note: 100%-recycled paperboard mill built 1947; Caraustar was headquartered here for decades. Greif acquired Caraustar in 2019; the mill is still operating.
